scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp (with @ngwes/mini-fp), write a weather widget flow with three stages that run one after the other over `{ ip: string; city?: string; forecast?: Forecast; html?: string }`: locate the city with `geo.cityOf(ip): Promise<string | undefined>` (fails with { tag: 'unknown-location' } when there is none), fetch the forecast with `weather.forecastFor(city): Promise<Forecast | undefined>` (fails with { tag: 'no-forecast' }), then render the HTML. An unknown location must not fail the widget: the flow goes on with the city 'Paris' and still fetches and renders its forecast. Any other failure stops the flow. Exceptions become { tag: 'crash', cause } and overwritten values { tag: 'conflict', keys }. Write `widget(ip: string): Promise<string>` that returns the HTML or 'error: <tag>'.
criteria: Handles 'unknown-location' in the failure hook (onLeft) by returning right (or Either.right) of a context with city set to 'Paris'
The recovered context is spread from the context the hook received (for example { ...ctx, city: 'Paris' }), not a new object that drops ip
The failure hook returns left(error) for every error other than 'unknown-location'
The locate stage returns the 'unknown-location' failure as a left; the 'Paris' default is not applied inside that stage or with try/catch

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp with @ngwes/mini-fp 2, write the hook configuration for an import flow over `{ fileName: string; rows?: string[]; imported?: number }` with the error type `type ImportError = { tag: 'crash'; message: string; cause: unknown } | { tag: 'conflict'; keys: ReadonlyArray<string> } | { tag: 'invalid-row'; line: number }`. The stages call third-party parsers that may throw anything: Error objects, plain strings, or nothing at all (`throw undefined`, `Promise.reject()`). A thrown value must stop the run with a 'crash' error whose message is readable in every one of those cases. An overwritten value stops the run with a 'conflict' error.
criteria: The exception hook returns left of a { tag: 'crash', ... } object, never left(exception) or left of the raw thrown value
Builds message with an instanceof Error check (or an equivalent type guard) and a String(...) or fixed-text fallback for other values, not with an unchecked (exception as Error).message
Keeps the thrown value in the error's cause field
The exception hook does not rethrow, so a thrown value ends as a left result

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, a document flow over `{ docId: string; markdown?: string; html?: string; lastModified?: Date }` has stages that each set `lastModified` to the current time after doing their work, so a later stage replaces the date an earlier one wrote. That rewrite is expected: the run must go on with the stage's new date. Any other overwrite of a value an earlier stage wrote is a bug and must stop the run with { tag: 'conflict', keys }. Exceptions become { tag: 'crash', cause }. Write the hook configuration.
criteria: When lastModified is the only conflicting key, the conflict hook returns right of the context the stage returned (its third argument, for example right(next)), not right of the context the stage received
The conflict hook returns left({ tag: 'conflict', keys }) when any key other than lastModified conflicts
The decision is made from the keys the hook receives (for example keys.every((key) => key === 'lastModified')), not by accepting every conflict
Does not avoid the conflict by changing the stages or the context type (for example removing lastModified or making it a new key per stage)
